grounding.preview:
The applicable procedure is for equipment-part and maintenance purchase requests, including a CIP pump mechanical seal kit. First document the equipment/part identifier, observed need, timing, operational and safety impact, and existing evidence. The equipment team then records the technical need, specifications, compatibility, alternatives, operating constraints, and unresolved technical items. The purchasing team reviews master data, inventory/supply status, supplier conditions, quotation-related information, and purchase-request status. Manufacturing planning reviews production, material readiness, line, and operational impact. Budget and cost matters may be reviewed by Finance or Business Planning when relevant, but budget allocation or approval is not defined as part of this review. After all applicable evidence is accumulated, an authorized person makes the final decision on formal submission, approval, external action, or purchase authorization. Supplier confirmation, budget allocation, purchase approval, purchase order, and system execution remain separate procedures and are not authorized by these SOPs alone.

SOP sources: SOP-01; SOP-02; SOP-03; SOP-04

grounding.preview:
For an additional order of an existing raw material such as strawberry concentrate, the requesting department should provide the item identification, reason for additional ordering, quantity and demand basis, required-by date, and unresolved items to Procurement. Procurement reviews master data, inventory, reservations, demand, inbound plans, supply conditions, and existing purchase-request status, distinguishing shortages, delays, and unverifiable information. Manufacturing Planning then reviews production-plan and material-readiness impact. Specification, quality, safety, or allergen-related review is not defined as a mandatory base step; it is handed to the responsible function only when an actual specification, quality, or safety issue is confirmed. The retrieved context does not provide price-review procedures, approval thresholds or limits, or detailed purchase-requisition/purchase-order authorization rules. Formal purchase-request submission, approval, supplier confirmation, contracting, ordering, ERP changes, and external execution remain separate decisions for an authorized person. An agent is limited to read-only evidence review and handoff: it must not execute procurement, approve, place an order, or modify external systems.

SOP sources: SOP-01; SOP-02; SOP-03
